assumptions: Durable resume may occur after a host reboot; the supplied interfaces do not restrict saved process identities to the current boot.
Workers remain in their initial process group, and the supervisor is single-threaded, as specified.
checks: Reviewed the supplied launch, signal deferral, cleanup, recovery and lock code without tools or external inspection.
Checked recovery identity comparisons against ordinary stale-state scenarios.
Treated the reported 141 passing tests and supplied test names as supporting evidence only; test bodies were not supplied.
issues: Persisted process identity is not bound to a host boot. process_identity records only pid, state, pgid and start_ticks; Master.recover_process and _stop_recovered_group establish ownership using pid, pgid and start_ticks. Linux start_ticks measures time since boot, so after a reboot an unrelated process-group leader can match a stale saved tuple. Recovery would then obtain valid pidfds for that unrelated group and STOP/KILL it. Pidfds stabilize the selected process but do not establish that it belongs to the previous invocation. Repair: durably record the Linux boot ID with the worker identity and compare it before inspecting or signalling saved PIDs. A different boot proves the prior local processes cannot remain alive; archive that record without signalling current processes. Records lacking a boot identity must fail closed or follow an explicitly reviewed migration.
next_actions: Add boot identity to durable process registration and recovery ownership checks.
Add regression coverage for a stale record from another boot whose PID, PGID and start ticks match a current process, verifying that no signal is sent; also cover records without boot identity.
Rerun lifecycle verification and obtain a fresh review of the repaired code.
residuals: The on_spawn implementation, recovery call ordering under the writer lock, and atomic persistence implementation are supplied only as interface descriptions. Their implementations were not independently checked.
Initial-group containment and the exclusion of uncatchable termination between fork and durable registration remain accepted scope limitations.
Source-panel checks and internal phase acceptance do not establish accounting correctness, scientific validity or human acceptance.
steps: Traced ordinary launch and handled-interruption cleanup.
Traced recovery ownership checks, membership freezing and stable-handle signalling.
Identified a stale-state ownership defect across host boots.
summary: Recovery can signal an unrelated process after reboot because durable process identities omit boot identity. Revise the recovery identity contract before acceptance.
